## gitshift gpg-keygen

🔐 Generate and manage GPG keys for commit signing

### Synopsis

Generate GPG keys with proper parameters and manage them within gitshift.
This command handles:
- GPG key generation with custom parameters
- Proper key configuration for Git commit signing
- Integration with gitshift account system
- Public key export for adding to Git platforms

The generated keys can be used with any Git platform:
- GitHub (github.com and GitHub Enterprise)
- GitLab (gitlab.com and self-hosted)
- Any Git platform supporting GPG signatures

```
gitshift gpg-keygen [account-alias] [flags]
```

### Examples

```
  # Generate GPG key for GitHub account
  gitshift gpg-keygen work-github

  # Generate key with custom email
  gitshift gpg-keygen myaccount --email user@company.com

  # Generate ECC key instead of RSA
  gitshift gpg-keygen myaccount --type ECC

  # Generate key with 2-year expiration
  gitshift gpg-keygen myaccount --expire-date 2y

  # Enable GPG signing automatically for this account
  gitshift gpg-keygen myaccount --enable
```

### Options

```
      --bits int             Key size in bits (RSA: 2048/4096, ignored for ECC) (default 4096)
      --email string         Email for GPG key (must match verified email on Git platform)
      --enable               Automatically enable GPG commit signing for this account
      --expire-date string   Key expiration (0=never, 1y=1 year, 2y=2 years, etc.) (default "0")
  -f, --force                Overwrite existing GPG key if present
  -h, --help                 help for gpg-keygen
      --type string          GPG key type (RSA, ECC, DSA) (default "RSA")
```

### Options inherited from parent commands

```
      --config string   config file (default is $HOME/.config/gitshift/config.yaml)
```
